q: 1. The point of contra flexure is a point where
explain: The point of contraflexure (or inflection) is the location in a structural member where the bending moment changes from positive (sagging) to negative (hogging) or vice versa.

q: 2. When shear force at a point is zero, then bending moment is... at that point.
explain: Mathematically, V = dM/dx. If the derivative (V) is zero, the function (M) is at a local maximum or minimum.

q: 3. In a simply supported beam carrying uniformly distributed load w per unit length, the point of contraflexure
options: lies in the centre of the beam
lies at the ends of the beam
depends upon the length of beam
explain: In a simply supported beam with downward UDL, the entire beam experiences sagging (positive BM). Since the sign never changes, there is no point of contraflexure.

q: 4. When there is a sudden increase or decrease in shear force diagram between any two points, it indicates that there is a
options: point load at the two points
no loading between the two points
uniformly distributed load between the two points
uniformly varying load between the two points
explain: A vertical jump in the shear force diagram always corresponds to the application of a concentrated (point) load at 그 point.

q: 5. When the shear force diagram is a parabolic curve between two points, it indicates that there is a
options: point load at the two points
no loading between the two points
uniformly distributed load between the two points
uniformly varying load between the two points
explain: If the loading is linear (uniformly varying), the shear force (its integral) will be a 2nd-degree parabolic curve.

q: 6. In a beam where shear force changes sign, the bending moment will be
explain: A change in sign in the SFD indicates that the SF passes through zero, which identifies the location of the maximum bending moment.

q: 7. The point of contraflexure occurs in
explain: Overhanging beams typically experience hogging over the supports and sagging in the span, creating points where the bending moment must pass through zero.

q: 8. The number of reaction components possible at a hinge on rollers supports is
explain: A roller support only resists movement perpendicular to the surface it sits on, providing exactly one vertical reaction component.

q: 9. The number of reaction components possible at a hinged end for a general loading is
explain: A hinged (pinned) support prevents horizontal and vertical displacement but allows rotation, resulting in two reaction components (Rx and Ry).

q: 10. The number of reaction components possible at a fixed or built in end for a general loading
explain: A fixed support prevents all movement (vertical, horizontal, and rotation), providing three reactions: vertical force, horizontal force, and a bending moment.

q: 11. A simply supported beam is subjected to a pure moment. This will be resisted through
options: a moment reaction at hinged end
a moment reaction at hinge on rollers end
a couple formed by the reaction from the two supports
external support capable of resisting moment
explain: Since simple supports cannot provide moment reactions, the applied moment is balanced by a couple consisting of two equal and opposite vertical reactions at the supports.

q: 12. A cantilever beam is the one which is supported with
options: one end hinge and other on rollers
one end fixed and the other on rollers
one end fixed and the other free
explain: A cantilever is defined by having one end entirely fixed (built-in) and the other end completely unsupported (free).

q: 13. A horizontal beam with both the ends hinged will be statically determinate for this type of loadings
explain: If both ends are hinged, there are 4 unknown reactions. For purely vertical loads, horizontal reactions are zero, reducing unknowns and making it determinate with basic equilibrium equations.

q: 14. A beam is said to be in general, stable and statically determinate for general loading when the number of reaction components is
explain: In 2D space, there are 3 equations of equilibrium (ΣFx, ΣFy, ΣM). A structure with 3 independent reaction components is statically determinate.

q: 15. The shear force on a simply supported beam is proportional to
options: algebraic sum of the transverse forces of the section
explain: By definition, the shear force at any section of a beam is the algebraic sum of all external transverse forces acting on either side of that section.

q: 16. A cantilever beam carrying a uniformly distributed load W over its full length is propped at its free end... BM will be zero at its free end also at
explain: For a propped cantilever with UDL, the point of zero bending moment (contraflexure) occurs at a distance of 3/4L from the fixed end (or 1/4L from the prop).

q: 17. A simply supported beam carrying a UDL... is propped at the centre... The reaction of the prop will be
explain: By equating the downward deflection of a SS beam due to UDL (5wL⁴/384EI) to the upward deflection due to the prop (PL³/48EI), the prop reaction is found to be 5/8 of the total load W.

q: 18. A uniform girder simply supported at its ends... propped at the centre so as to neutralize the deflection. The net B.M. at the centre will be
explain: With a prop reaction of 5/8W, the net BM at the center becomes (WL/8) - (5/8W * L/4) = WL/32.

q: 19. The moment diagram for a cantilever whose free end is subjected to a bending moment, will be a
explain: If a constant moment is applied at the end, the internal bending moment is uniform throughout the length, resulting in a rectangular BMD.

q: 20. The moment diagram for a cantilever carrying linearly varying load from zero at its free end and to maximum at the fixed end will be
explain: Since the load is linear (1st degree), the shear force is parabolic (2nd degree) and the bending moment is a cubic parabola (3rd degree).

q: 21. The moment diagram for a cantilever which is subjected to a uniformly distributed load will be a
explain: For a UDL (0th degree), the shear force is linear (1st degree) and the bending moment is parabolic (2nd degree).

q: 22. The moment diagram for a cantilever carrying a concentrated load at its free end, will be
explain: The bending moment varies linearly from zero at the free end to (W * L) at the fixed support, resulting in a triangular Bending Moment Diagram (BMD).

q: 23. Shear force for a cantilever carrying a uniformly distributed load over its length, is
explain: The shear force at any section x from the free end is (w * x). This linear relationship (1st degree) forms a right-angled triangle.

q: 24. When a rectangular beam is loaded longitudinally, shear develops on
explain: Longitudinal or complementary shear stress is developed across every horizontal plane of the beam to maintain equilibrium against the varying bending stresses.

q: 25. A simply supported beam is subjected to a udl of intensity W/m throughout the length of the span. The B.M. diagram will be a
explain: A UDL produces a 2nd-degree curve (parabola) for the bending moment, with the peak value at the center being wl²/8.

q: 26. The bending moment in a beam will be maximum where
explain: The maximum bending moment occurs at the section where the shear force is zero or changes its sign.

q: 27. The slope of curve of B.M. diagram at any section will be equal to
options: the slope of moment at that section
the slope of S.F. diagram at that section
the ordinate of S.F. diagram at that section
the area of S.F. diagram starting from any one end
explain: The rate of change of bending moment (dM/dx) at a section is equal to the shear force (V) at that section.

q: 28. A simply supported beam is subjected to a uniformly varying load with zero intensity at the two ends increasing to W/m at the centre. the maximum S.F. is
explain: The total load is (1/2 * l * w). Since the loading is symmetrical, each reaction (Max SF) is half the total load: (1/2 * wl/2) = wl/4.

q: 29. A simply supported beam is subjected to a uniformly varying load with zero intensity at the two ends increasing to W/m at the centre. The max. B.M. will occur at
explain: For a symmetrical loading on a simply supported beam, the maximum bending moment always occurs at the mid-span (l/2 from either end).

q: 30. A simply supported beam is subjected to a uniformly varying load with zero intensity at the two ends increasing to W/m at the centre. The maximum B.M. will be equal to
explain: For this specific triangular loading (apex at center), the maximum bending moment at the mid-span is calculated as wl²/12.

q: 31. Which of the following end conditions permits the displacement in any direction and also rotation?
explain: A free end has no constraints; it can move horizontally, vertically, and rotate freely under load.

q: 32. Which of the following beams will have points of contraflexure? (self weight is negligible)
options: a simply supported beam with udl over entire span
a overhanging beam with loading only over supported span and not on overhangs
fixed beam subjected to concentrated load
cantilever subjected to uniformly varying loads
explain: Fixed beams develop hogging moments at the supports and sagging moments in the center, necessitating points of contraflexure where the BM is zero.

q: 33. A beam is said to have been subjected to a pure bending moment, when
options: the load is applied as a udl throughout the span
S.F. in a length is zero
the load is applied at the mid-span section only
explain: Pure bending occurs in a region where the shear force is zero, meaning the bending moment is constant over that length.

q: 34. The slope of the B.M. diagram change its sign when
explain: The slope of BMD is the Shear Force. If SF changes sign (from positive to negative), the slope of the BM curve changes from increasing to decreasing.

q: 35. A bending moment may be defined as
options: arithmetic sum of the moments of all the forces on either side of the section
arithmetic sum of the forces on either sides of the section
algebraic sum of the moments of all the forces on either side of the section
explain: The internal bending moment at a section is the algebraic sum of the moments of all external forces acting on one side of the section.

q: 36. If Z and I are the section modulus and moment of inertia of the section, the shear force F and bending moment M at a section are related by
explain: The fundamental differential relationship between bending moment and shear force is that F (or V) is the derivative of M with respect to distance x.

q: 37. At either end of a plane frame, maximum number of possible transverse shear forces, are
explain: In a 2D plane frame member, there is only one transverse (perpendicular to the axis) shear force component at any section.

q: 38. At either end of a plane frame, maximum number of possible bending moments, are
explain: In a 2D plane frame, bending occurs only in the plane of the frame, resulting in a single bending moment component (Mz).

q: 39. the shape of the bending moment diagram over the length of a beam, having no external load, is always
explain: With no external load between two points, the shear force is constant (horizontal line), making the bending moment linear (inclined line).

q: 40. The shape of the bending moment diagram over the length of a beam, carrying a uniformly distributed load is always
explain: UDL (constant) leads to a linear SFD, which integrates into a 2nd-degree parabolic curve for the BMD.

q: 41. The shape of the bending moment diagram over the length of a beam, carrying a uniformly increasing load, is always
explain: A uniformly increasing load (1st degree) leads to a parabolic SFD (2nd degree) and a cubical parabolic BMD (3rd degree).

q: 42. The maximum bending moment due to a moving load on a simply supported beam, occurs
explain: For a single concentrated moving load, the absolute maximum bending moment at any section always occurs when the load is placed directly over that section.

q: 43. For a simply supported beam with a central load, the bending moment is
explain: For a simply supported beam of length L with a central point load P, the bending moment increases linearly from zero at the supports to a maximum value of PL/4 at the center.

q: 44. For a cantilever with a uniformly distributed load W over its entire length L, the maximum bending moment is
explain: In a cantilever beam with a UDL, the maximum bending moment occurs at the fixed support and is calculated as (Total Load × Distance to CG), which is W × (L/2) = WL/2.

q: 45. The bending moment is maximum on a section where shearing force
explain: According to the relationship dM/dx = V, the bending moment (M) reaches a local maximum or minimum value where the shear force (V) is zero or changes its sign.

q: 46. A beam is said to be of uniform strength, if
options: B.M. is same throughout the beam
shear stress is same throughout the beam
deflection is same throughout the beam
bending stress is same at every section along its longitudinal axis
explain: A beam of uniform strength is designed by varying its cross-section such that the maximum fiber stress (bending stress) remains constant at every section along its length.

q: 47. In a continuous bending moment curve the point where it changes sign, is called
explain: The point where the bending moment changes from sagging (+) to hogging (-) or vice versa is known by all these terms; it is the location where the curvature of the beam changes.

q: 48. For a beam, if fundamental equations of statics are not sufficient to determine all the reactive forces at the supports, the structure is said to be
explain: Statically indeterminate structures have more unknown support reactions or internal forces than the available equations of equilibrium (ΣH=0, ΣV=0, ΣM=0).

q: 49. If the beam is supported so that there are only three unknown reactive elements at the supports. These can be determined by using the following fundamental equation of statics
explain: For a 2D structure, the three independent equations of equilibrium are the summation of horizontal forces, vertical forces, and moments about any point.

q: 50. For a beam having fixed ends, the unknown element of the reactions, is
options: horizontal component at one end and vertical component at the other
horizontal and vertical components at both the ends
explain: A fixed support prevents translation in both directions and rotation, resulting in three unknowns per support (Horizontal, Vertical, and Moment).
